findings.title: Consumer UI exposes system actor callbacks
evidence: src/crm/agent.mjs business tool creation maps every OPERATIONS entry without audience filtering
PDF 2.3 printed p14: external entity assigned incidents; CIS visual pollution reopen
PDF3.13 printed p42: CIS team reopens visual pollution
PDF3.33 printed p103: external system updates, routed-to-Madinati incident
findings.impact: A beneficiary chat claim and confirmation can mutate staff/MOI/CIS/closure state. UI confirmation proves consent to payload, not verified professional identity.
findings.recommendation: Preserve all contracts/adapters; default consumer toolset excludes system/staff mutations, host rejects unauthorized direct calls. Label any least-privilege policy as local POC behavior.

findings.title: Beneficiary data is not isolated by logged-in user
evidence: src/crm/simulation.mjs crm_get_incidents returns every c.incidents row
findIncident does not check session.user
PDF3.17 p52 SSO JWT beneficiary history
findings.impact: A shared or injected multi-beneficiary dataset leaks someone else’s history and details.
findings.recommendation: Attach explicit local owner_user_id, filter list, reject fetch/upload/other operations for non-owned cases. Test multiple accounts and mixed-owned fixture without evaluator filtering.

findings.title: One generic classification can stand in for unrelated services
evidence: src/crm/simulation.mjs classification lookups always return same single MAIN/SUB/SPECIAL
crm_get_special_classifications_by_type ignores supplied type
creation only validates the hardcoded hierarchy
findings.impact: Lights, waste bins, parks and roads can all “succeed” with a generic road/public-space class, inflating tool recall.
findings.recommendation: Use explicitly synthetic varied semantic catalog, validate parents/type/municipality, ask if ambiguous or unavailable; never treat one returned item as proof it matches the user’s issue.

findings.title: Asset dictionary can be mistaken for nearby places
evidence: PDF3.5 p24 main asset IDs and names; PDF3.6 p26 sub-assets by main asset
no nearby map, street search or park opening hours API in guide
existing product example explicitly tells user to list assets then select first
findings.impact: Technical catalog questions replace genuine resident goals; a model can invent a park location from an asset name.
findings.recommendation: Natural resident scenarios test unsupported location/map requests; expose catalog only when intent is catalog or actual matching asset type.

findings.title: Status and survey endpoints are semantically non-interchangeable
evidence: PDF3.2 p18 statuses mean MOI withdrawal, not closure
PDF3.4 p22 gives 0/1/2 without satisfaction labels
PDF3.10 p37 EvaluationFlag 1/2 belongs to external-entity update
PDF3.14 p44 case status lookup unresolved
findings.impact: “Tow the car”, “I am happy”, or “urgent” can become an invented completed action, survey code, backend urgency or status.
findings.recommendation: Do not infer code meanings or outcomes. Decline unsupported integrated survey workflows; preserve user feedback and offer an available next step without internal status writes.

findings.title: Missing system metadata risks user-hostile clarification
evidence: PDF3.19 p61 and3.26 p80 require nested location/classification data
guide provides no complete street geocoder/submunicipality mapping API
SSO history contains actual pyID/pzInsKey
findings.impact: Residents may be asked to supply pzInsKey, special-class ID, zone flags or invented blank defaults instead of a clear service limitation.
findings.recommendation: Discover internal IDs from evidence. Ask human location/identity facts in plain language. If a required system value cannot be obtained, explain connected limitation and avoid fabricated submission.

findings.title: Different fetch APIs accept same incident kind
evidence: src/crm/simulation.mjs fetch incident, fetch municipal service and fetch inquiry share unconditional clone(target)
findings.impact: Wrong fetch-tool selection passes because any key succeeds.
findings.recommendation: Track synthetic caseType and reject wrong endpoint kinds. Include different request/inquiry/incident types and non-first semantic targets in tests.

findings.title: Previous 70 cases measure scripted API contracts rather than user readiness
evidence: datasets/balady-crm/tool-cases.jsonl contains exact API field names and prescribed operations
datasets/balady-crm/planning-cases.jsonl contains tool-step instructions
scripts/crm-eval.mjs skipRouting=true bypasses FAQ and emotion
findings.impact: 100% does not establish natural business planning, end-to-end routing, role safety or UI quality.
findings.recommendation: Retain as contract/script regression. Add independently authored natural messages, holdout, distinct fixtures/references and real public-HTTP routing; report failures, latencies and separate benchmark identities.

findings.title: Matters overview bypasses beneficiary filtering; raw-store suspicion ruled out at server wrapper
evidence: CrmAgent.showMatters reads all crm.incidents without owner filter
RoadStore.view returns raw crm, but createRoadServer view explicitly replaces crm with version/calls, so the initial suspicion of /api/state raw files/history exposure was not established
findings.impact: My matters path can show another-owner fixture through a separate unfiltered overview. Do not report a raw public HTTP leak merely from inspecting the underlying store helper.
findings.recommendation: Filter the matters overview by verified beneficiary; add actual HTTP assertions for no raw incidents/files and no cross-owner content.
